title: Dueling Medical Marijuana Initiative Drives Planned for Washington, DC

content_html_sanitized:
See: DC Medical marijuana initiative supporters fail to get enough valid signatures on their petitions

After falling only a few hundred signatures short of their goal, medical marijuana activist Steve Michael of ACT-UP DC said that they have now refiled the initiative, which would legalize the possession, use, distribution and cultivation of marijuana if recommended by a physician for illnesses such as AIDS, cancer and glaucoma. With the expected Board approval in January, volunteers could begin seeking signatures in early February. To get the measure on the September ballot, they would have to turn in signatures by May 15.

In the meantime, Americans for Medical Rights (AMR), a California group that ran the Proposition 215 medical marijuana initiative there last year, is launching its own ballot initiative in the District. AMR has filed a measure with the elections board and hired a D.C. lawyer and a professional organizer to drum up support. Dave Fratello, a spokesman for the group, said AMR plans to spend at least $40,000 and perhaps as much as $500,000 to get its initiative passed.

Unfortunately there is a split in the movement. ACT-UP is staunchly opposed to a provision in AMR's initiative that would require medical marijuana users to register with the D.C. government and carry identification cards. "If they continue with their initiative, there will be a war, and we will win," Michael said. "The people of D.C. can't let these big-money outsiders come in and make local law." (Ed. note: That never happens in DC) He added: "If the [elections] board allows both of us to gather signatures, voters are going to be confused. Everyone agrees on that."
